item.title: 1.1.99-beta.6
item.description:
1.1.99-beta.6: Stability & Conflict Management

New Features:

  • Conflict Detection:
    • Added a detection system to identify if other menu bar managers (e.g., Ice, Bartender, Hidden Bar) are running simultaneously.
    • Displays a warning alert to prevent potential display issues caused by multiple managers.
    • Users can now choose to continue anyway or quit Thaw upon detection.
  • Enhanced Layout Persistence:
    • Implemented a save/restore mechanism for menu bar items that macOS does not natively remember, such as Stats.app.
    • Items are now identified by persistent tags (namespace:title) rather than volatile PIDs.
    • Added a 500ms settle delay during restoration to allow the macOS UI to stabilize before moving items.

Improvements & Fixes:

  • Memory & Performance:
    • Added autoreleasepool blocks to menu bar operations to prevent memory leaks.
    • Implemented a 10-second timeout to reset stale restoration flags, preventing the app from getting stuck in a "restoring" state.
  • Event Handling:
    • Thaw now listens for NSWorkspace.didLaunchApplicationNotification to automatically relocate menu bar items from newly launched apps.
  • Internationalization (i18n):
    • Added Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR) translations.
    • Added Turkish (tr) language support.
    • Updated German (de) translations and added missing developer comments for translators.

item.title: 1.1.99-beta.5
item.description:
1.1.99-beta.5: Layout Persistence & Performance Refinement

New Features:

  • Persistent Layouts:
    • Added the ability to restore menu bar items to their saved sections automatically.

Improvements & Fixes:

  • Cache Optimization:
    • Significantly improved SourcePIDCache efficiency and reliability for smoother background processing.
    • Optimized PID cache updates and cleanup routines within the Menu Bar Item Service.
    • Enhanced memory management by adding autoreleasepool to cache cleanup tasks.
    • Refined the negative cache reset logic to ensure more accurate process tracking.
  • Menu Bar & Events:
    • Fixed an issue where clicking visible section items would incorrectly reopen hidden sections.
    • Improved click detection by querying fresh window bounds from the Window Server immediately before checking click locations.

item.title: 1.1.99-beta.4
item.description:
1.1.99-beta.4: Mission Control Support & Efficiency

New Features:

  • Mission Control Integration:
    • The menu bar overlay now hides instantly during Mission Control and App Exposé for a seamless system transition.
    • Implemented an invisible "probe" window and high-frequency timer to reliably track system-wide window transformations.
  • Enhanced Search Window:
    • Added a magnifying glass icon and clickable edit buttons to the search panel bottom bar.
    • Improved keyboard handling: pressing Esc now clears the search field or closes the window if the field is empty.
    • Search results now feature a periodic refresh loop to keep animated icons, like sync spinners, live while the panel is open.
  • Advanced Customization:
    • Added a configurable "Icon refresh rate" slider (1–30 fps) to Advanced settings, allowing users to tune the live refresh interval.
    • The application now persists and restores specific item orders per-section for more reliable layout management.

Improvements & Fixes:

  • Performance & Battery Life:
    • Rewrote the transparency check engine to read alpha bytes directly from memory, eliminating constant allocations during the refresh loop.
    • Reduced interaction latency by 100-500ms when clicking Ice Bar items by skipping redundant input pause polling.
    • Moved initial cache preloading to background tasks to ensure smoother UI transitions in the settings and search panels.
  • Menu Bar Stability:
    • Fixed a race condition that could cause missing menu bar items after a drag operation.
    • Improved stability for external drags and suppressed caching during active move operations to prevent layout flickering.
  • Bug Fixes & Maintenance:
    • Removed debug log spam from computed properties that were evaluated dozens of times per render pass.
    • Excluded internal control items from image captures to eliminate unnecessary failure and retry cycles.
    • Updated the Sparkle framework to version 2.9.0 for improved update reliability.

1.1.0: Breaking the Ice

⚠️ Important Note: Due to essential internal changes in how Thaw manages menu bar items, your current icon positions will be reset to "Always Visible." I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience, but this manual re-adjustment is unavoidable to ensure future stability.

Localization Support:

Thaw is now available in 12 languages with 100% completion. A huge thank you to our community contributors:

  • Chinese (Simplified): by @PiCpo
  • Chinese (Traditional): by @7a6163
  • Dutch: by @SeBr28
  • French: by @PipaCode
  • German: by @Mutzki13
  • Hungarian: by @johnnybakucz
  • Indonesian: by @volcbs
  • Italian: by @zichichi
  • Korean: by @YuriHan
  • Spanish: by @diazdesandi
  • Thai: by @priesdelly

Changes and Fixes:

  • Multi-Monitor Support: Improved app menu hiding logic to correctly account for screen edges and active menu bars across multiple monitors.
  • Ultra-wide Monitor Fix: Resolved an issue where menu bar items were incorrectly included in calculations, which previously caused "Hidden" and Always Hidden" items to appear incorrectly on the left side of ultra-wide screens.
  • Refined Notch Detection: Implemented auxiliaryTopLeftArea for more accurate notch detection and added an option to enable the IceBar only on displays with a notch.
  • Immediate UI Updates: Menubar shapes (split/full) now update instantly when settings are changed, eliminating the previous 30-second delay.
  • Display-Specific Layouts: Fixed an issue where menu bar items from primary displays were incorrectly included in trailing path calculations for external monitors.
  • Performance Optimizations: Reduced CPU usage by debouncing image cache updates, adding polling delays, and skipping background timer tasks when panels are hidden.
  • Simplified Settings: Removed the redundant "temporary item delay" setting as the smart rehide logic now handles these cases automatically.
  • Thaw Bar Scaling Fix: Resolved a scaling issue in the Thaw Bar by clamping the menu bar content height and capping item height to ensure consistent rendering.
  • New Interaction: Added the ability to double-click directly on the menu bar to reveal the "Always Hidden" section.

1.0.0: The Official Release

Thaw has reached its first stable milestone! This release consolidates all the progress from the beta period into a polished, reliable menu bar manager.

Latest Improvements (since beta 4):

  • Enhanced Reliability: Stabilized HIDEventManager logic to prevent "show on hover" and "show on click" from stopping after repeated use and prevent saving chevron divider position which could leave Thaw in an unusable state.
  • UI Polish: Condensed the menu bar tooltip for a cleaner look and added explicit double-click instructions.
  • System Safety: Improved thread safety by synchronizing access to the cursor hide count.
  • Apple Menu Fix: Refined synthetic press offsets to ensure Thaw never accidentally triggers the Apple menu.

Highlights from the Journey to 1.0:

  • The Big Thaw: Successfully forked and rebranded with a new identity, app icon, and independent bundle ID (com.stonerl.Thaw).
  • Ice Migration: Built-in support to import your old settings and control item positions from Ice.
  • Advanced Control: Introduced "Double-Click to Reveal" for always-hidden items and "Smart Rehide" strategies.
  • Modern macOS Support: Optimized for stability on macOS 26.
  • Performance: Faster icon caching, display-aware state refreshing, and thread-safe operations.

Known Issues:

If you are currently on macOS 14 or 15, please be aware that Thaw currently has some known bugs regarding temporary icons in the floating Thaw bar.

I am actively investigating these issues and will release a fix as soon as possible. You can track the progress of this issue here: GitHub Issue #1.

Thank you for all the feedback during the beta period that made this release possible!
